requirements.text: they should go to the first triage group(smallest) that handles cases, but make sure that group doesn't already have too many (must be under 6 open cases)
requirements.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM customer_case WHERE case_id = 53 AND assignment_group_id = 3
requirements.source: Case moved to Case Triage and in_progress
assumptions: Acme is account 3 (Acme Systems); its critical cases in state new are 52 and 53
case 53 (product 159) qualifies: entitlement 24 is active, enterprise, for product 159, on contract 8 (active, 2025-09-18 to 2027-04-05)
case 52 names no product, so coverage for a specified product cannot be confirmed and it is left out
'first triage group (smallest)' read as the lowest group id among the Case Triage groups (3, 23, 43, 63): group 3, Case Triage, type support
group 3 has 5 open cases on the seed (588, 667, 687, 1010, 1012; not closed, canceled or resolved), under the limit of 6
assigned_to is not fixed by the request and is not tested

requirements.text: Change those cases to show they're being worked on
requirements.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM customer_case WHERE case_id = 53 AND state = 'in_progress'
requirements.source: Case moved to Case Triage and in_progress
assumptions: 'being worked on' is state in_progress; the policy allows new to in_progress

requirements.text: Check active enterprise support coverage for specified product in cases
requirements.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM customer_case WHERE case_id = 52 AND assignment_group_id = 40 AND state = 'new'
assumptions: case 52 is critical and new for Acme but names no product, so coverage for a specified product cannot be confirmed; it is neither routed nor started
keeping its seed group 40 and state new also covers the benchmark's narrower test (not both group 3 and in_progress)

requirements.text: Look at critical priority cases that are new for the Acme account
requirements.selector: account_id = 3 AND case_id NOT IN (52, 53) AND (priority = 'critical' OR state = 'new')
requirements.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM customer_case WHERE account_id = 3 AND case_id NOT IN (52, 53) AND (priority = 'critical' OR state = 'new') AND assignment_group_id IS NOT 3 AND state IS NOT 'in_progress'
assumptions: boundary of the selector: Acme's critical cases that are not new (60 pending, 61 resolved, 68 and 69 canceled) and its new cases that are not critical (54, 70, 71, 72) are outside the set; none may go to group 3 or to in_progress
IS NOT is used because case 70 has no assignment group, and NULL <> 3 would drop it from the count

disagreement: selector and cells: one pass cases 60, 61, 68 and 69 with group not 3 and state not in_progress (4 rows), the other every Acme case except 52 and 53 with no row in group 3 (0 rows); chose Acme's critical or new cases except 52 and 53, testing both group and state (8 rows), because those are the rows a reading that drops either 'critical' or 'new' would sweep in, and each of the two readings alone misses half of them or leaves the state untested

verify entitlements.evidence: entitlement 24 (account 3, product 159, active, enterprise) exists on the seed and no listed tool writes the entitlement table; the check reads a fact the agent only consults

Verify under 6 open cases related to gro.evidence: the request's limit applies before the move ('doesn't already have too many'): group 3 has 5 open cases on the seed (588, 667, 687, 1010, 1012); once case 53 moves in as in_progress, as the request asks, the correct final count is 6, so an expected count of 5 contradicts 'Case moved to Case Triage and in_progress'

No updation for case_id 52.evidence: case 52 names no product, so it is not one of the cases to move or start; the check's count of 0 holds on the correct final state and nothing in the request, policy or seed contradicts it. The requirement carrying it tests more: that case 52 keeps both its group (40) and its state (new)

notes:
Reading of the case set: case 52 is left out because the request asks for coverage of the product specified in the case and case 52 names none. Account 3 also holds active account-wide enterprise entitlements (15, 18, 21, product_id NULL), which the policy lets cover any product; under that reading case 52 would qualify too, but group 3 would then pass from 5 to 7 open cases, breaking the under-6 limit after the first move, so the single-case reading is the consistent one.
'Smallest' could also mean fewest members; among the Case Triage groups with under 6 open cases (3 with 16 members, 43 with 14; 63 has 8 members but 7 open cases, 23 is a vendor group with 9) that reading would pick group 43. The lowest id, group 3, is used, as 'first' suggests and as the benchmark check expects.
Product 159 is in lifecycle_state retired and installed product 17 on case 53 is retired; the policy bars attaching retired items to new cases, but the case already carries them and the request only routes and starts it, so the move is not blocked.
The policy's SLA alignment on moving to in_progress is already met on the seed (case 53 has case_sla 105 and 106 for critical response and resolution, definitions 1 and 6) and no listed tool writes case_sla, so it is not a requirement.
The benchmark's description says assigned_to stays NULL for case 53 and that no critical new cases remain for account 3; its query tests neither, the request names a group and no user, and case 52 stays new, so neither is tested.
disagreement: value: the boundary stay on Acme's cases outside the set: one pass selected the four critical cases that are not new and tested group and state, the other selected every other Acme case and tested group 3 only; chose the critical or new Acme cases outside the set with both group and state tested, the rows a loose reading of 'critical priority cases that are new' would sweep in.
disagreement: disposition: 'No updation for case_id 52': one pass kept it, the other repaired it as too loose; kept, because its count of 0 holds on the correct final state and no value in it is wrong, and the requirement that carries it tests the tighter condition.
